outcome: Composite adverse pregnancy outcome (fetal loss before 24 weeks, termination of pregnancy, stillbirth, infant death, major congenital anomaly)
Extended perinatal mortality (stillbirths and neonatal deaths)
Admission to special care baby unit
cohort: The study cohort included 27 women with twin pregnancies and pregestational diabetes (54 babies) and 6407 women with twin pregnancies without diabetes (12,814 babies) from a regional register.
finding: Maternal pregestational diabetes in twin pregnancies is associated with significantly increased rates of the composite adverse outcome and major congenital anomalies.
mod_finding: Twins of mothers with pregestational diabetes were more likely to be delivered by cesarean section (80.4% vs. 49.7%).
followup_time: Up to 1 year after birth for infant death, and up to 28 days for neonatal death.
